pr_title: drivers: i2c: stm32 driver V2 new timing calculation
pr_body:
This PR is implementing a new formula to calculate the I2C timing value from the I2C clock source and the bit rate.
Algorithm coming from https://github.com/ARMmbed/mbed-os/blob/master/targets/TARGET_STM/i2c_api.c

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/55535

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>
pr_comments:
stm32 I2C V2 FAST bitrate 
![stm32 I2C V2 fast](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/51417392/0d46a783-5e1f-4173-9497-68003a6a2d25)

stm32 I2C V2 STANDARD bitrate
![stm32 I2C V2 standard](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/51417392/7bc87b8f-b6f0-4991-8021-a60a1d458d97)
a second commit, to fix the compliance check warning and retrieve the original (correct) function

Rebase, fix macro to get the same timing value
STANDARD : 0xb0c03e40
FAST : 0xc041090f

> Please cleanup second commit message. Otherwise LGTM

done

Add a sample to calculate the I2C V2 timing value and then report to the I2C node in the Device Tree
```
I2C timing value, report to the DTS : 
timings = <160000000 I2C_BITRATE_FAST  0xC041090F>;
```

The i2C V2 driver does not embed the timing calculation code. 
Only when the CONFIG_I2C_STM32_V2_TIMING=y is set by the samples/boards/stm32/i2c_V2_timing/  is the timing value output on the console.

Rebase on 68365d5b67057c8e960a5168c2cf99f4b8c457c1

Includes the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/64422   with the get_config API
Change the sample

Running the samples/boards/stm32/i2c_config/ on the b_u585i_iot02a : 

```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.5.0-785-g6d149c663d59 ***
I2C timing value, report to the DTS :
timings = <160000000 I2C_BITRATE_FAST  0xC041090F>;
I2C config: I2C_BITRATE_FAST
```

Then to report to the board DTS for the i2c2 node : 
```
&i2c2 {
	timings = <160000000 I2C_BITRATE_FAST  0xC041090F>;
}
```

idem for bit rate  STANDARD and FAST_PLUS

issue_context.title: ST kit b_u585i_iot02a I2C clock frequency error
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
I added HTS221 register reading to blinky. Measured clock speed was 110 KHz and this is a little bit too much. I checked clocking and PLL is used (msi-pll-mode). I also checked dividers and everything seemed OK to my eyes.

Is there a bug at clock configuration or maybe a clock calibration missing ?

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. west build -p auto -b b_u585i_iot02a_ns samples\basic\blinky
2. west flash
3. boot and measure STMod+pin 7, I2C2_SCL
4. note that HTS221 is OK

**Expected behavior**
Freq should be max 100 KHz

**Impact**
Freq over I2C specification

**Logs and console output**

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Toolchain (e.g Zephyr SDK, ...)
 - latest codes from github
[blink.zip](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/10909330/blink.zip)

> Measured clock speed was about 110 KHz. I'am curious, was there any expectation that freq will be different ?

Thanks. No I wasn't expcting a different value, but since you mentionned the _ns target, it was worth checking.

When running the tests/drivers/i2c/i2c_target_api/  on the nucleo_u575zi_q, with  `I2C_BITRATE_STANDARD`,  the SCL  freq is measured at ~100kHz
However it seems that the formula in the stm32_i2c_configure_timing() function does not give a result of 400kHz for I2C_BITRATE_FAST when i2c input clock is SYSCLOCK or HSI 16MHz.
STM3CubeMX gives 0x00F08BFF for FAST_ mode (400kHz) clocked by the PLL1K (160MHz)  while stm32_i2c_configure_timing gives 0x40fc1228
Even for the 100kHz standard bitrate, the timing value differs from what the stm32CubeMx calculates.

Freq is now 100 kHz, great. I had to modify file, compiler problems. See zip file and search // text.
[i2c_ll_stm32_v2.zip](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/11905137/i2c_ll_stm32_v2.zip)

Two complementary ideas:
- A] Proposal is to set `timings` property as required.
Then provision a default `timings` table that would cover some common I2C freq/bitrate configuration.
Driver should return an error if the requested runtime configuration is not covered by `timings` table.
If error is generated, it is up to user to provide the correct timing (either from CubeMX or other method), as an overwrite of the default value.
- B] Implement https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/59815 with a specific feature switch (STM32_I2C_V2_GENERATE_TIMING), which could be enabled temporarily to generate and print the use case timing value. Once generated, back to A].

this PR started last year, so 2023 was pertinent at that time,
should we really  update this comment since this is a "internal" sample

This large buffer is bothering me. That's 128 struct of 5 32-bit words, so more than 2.5kB static memory.
This should not be permanent. I think it could be declared as a simple local variable in stm32_i2c_configure_timing, and then passed as argument to the other functions.
The same could be applied to this variable, though it is less important as it's only one word.
That piece looks suspicious. Is that a left over ?
This is to break the successive loops and avoid entering the macro I2C_LOOP_SDADEL  again if useless
